Cyberattacks — what is happening now and how to prepare · GOV RADAR
what is happening, and how to prepare

Hacking, DDoS and ransomware can stop power, money, water, food and healthcare. We separate real attacks from plain outages in incidents from September to November 2026, and set out what households, companies and governments can do now.
As of 2026-11-15 · Korean figures: MSIT/KISA H1 2026 cyber-threat report (30 Jul)
'Hacking' covers very different methods and harms. Each kind comes with real cases.
Encrypts or steals data and demands payment. Today it is often 'double extortion': steal first, then threaten to publish.
Real cases · Queens Public Library (Nov 2026) · Japanese cloud provider, 495 clients down (Oct 2026) · Asahi brewing halt (Sep 2025) · Colonial Pipeline (May 2021)
Floods a server with traffic from many devices until the service stops.
Main harm · Banking, payment and e-government sites unreachable
Real cases · Korea: 373 DDoS reports in H1 2026, up 56.7% (MSIT/KISA) · 7.7 DDoS (2009)
Malicious software that takes over devices or servers or steals data, including web shells (server back doors).
Main harm · Data theft, server takeover, a foothold for further attacks
Real cases · PHP flaw campaign targeting 216 servers in 10 countries, 30 in Korea (reported Nov 2026)
Tricks people with fake emails, texts or job offers to hand over accounts and access.
Main harm · Bank accounts, corporate systems and crypto wallets compromised
Real cases · Fake résumé sites used against 3 Korean organisations (Oct 2026, Kaspersky) · social engineering in the Binance theft (Oct 2026)
Gets into many companies at once through a supplier, outsourced service or software update.
Main harm · One breach hits dozens to thousands of client companies

Real cases · Via call-centre contractor MetaM, 22 finance and gaming firms (Nov 2026) · ~2,950 servers via a cPGuard update (Nov 2026) · 1,300+ npm package versions poisoned (Aug 2026) · SolarWinds (2020)
Changes the control signals and set-points of physical equipment such as water plants, refrigeration and power stations.
Main harm · Risk to drinking water, food waste, damage to medicines and blood, power cuts
Real cases · European supermarket refrigeration (Oct–Nov 2026) · French plasma freezers set to 110°C (Nov 2026) · Oldsmar water plant (2021) · Ukrainian grid (2015)
Disables the systems that actually run factories, logistics, ports and ships.
Main harm · Production lines, ports and shipping stopped
Real cases · Jaguar Land Rover plants halted ~5 weeks (Sep 2025) · Maersk and others hit by NotPetya (2017) · LNG carrier control-system fault, cyberattack suspected (Sep 2026, under investigation)
Takes over log-in, signing or approval steps to move money and crypto out.
Main harm · Loss of crypto and financial assets
Real cases · Binance ~$6.3bn (Oct 2026, FBI: North Korea-linked) · Bybit ~$1.5bn (Feb 2025) · Korean exchange hot wallet ~₩100m (Oct 2026)
Not about money: deletes data and wrecks systems so they are hard to restore.
Main harm · Loss of records, long recovery
Real cases · Russian host's cloud data wiped, 1,000+ servers checked by hand (Nov 2026) · medical-device maker's devices wiped (Mar 2026) · NotPetya (2017)
Jams or fakes GPS signals, or takes over alert apps to send false warnings.
Real cases · Ukraine's air-alert app used to send fake radiation and chemical alerts in Kyiv (Nov 2026) · KA-SAT satellite outage cut remote monitoring of European wind turbines (Feb 2022)
Goes after the side doors — lookup services, admin tools, outsourced SaaS, forgotten files — rather than the core system.
Main harm · Mass data leaks, entry into internal networks
Real cases · 16 Korean financial firms, ~100,000 records (as of Oct 2026) · Japanese member-lookup API abused, up to ~22.5m records (Oct 2026)
Uses AI to automate vulnerability scanning, exploit writing and intrusion at greater speed and scale.
Main harm · Dozens to hundreds of targets at once
Real cases · Group using AI tooling arrested after stealing 8.2m+ records from ~90 Korean firms (Oct 2026) · AI agents reported to breach 100+ websites (Oct 2026)

Recent incidents — real attacks vs plain outages
Suspected North Korea-linked group targets 216 servers via PHP flaw
Cipherma report: unpatched web servers targeted for web shells. Targets: US 49, Japan 47, India 31, Korea 30 (government, finance, telecom, logistics, manufacturing). Attackers claim 581 targets.
Leaks reported at a small-business fund, a university and a local-currency platform
· Not an attack so far. DHS: 'no indication of a threat or attack — a telecommunications outage'.
Tanker hits riverboat in New Orleans
Call-centre contractor hacked — 22 finance and gaming firms

MetaM, which runs customer service for 200+ firms, detected unauthorised access on 12 Nov and reported it to KISA. 22 clients affected, including exchange Coinone: names, phone, resident numbers, account numbers and passwords possibly exposed.
· Confirmed breach. No intrusion into Coinone's own trading or wallet systems found.
· Not an attack: server and infrastructure problems. Lesson: single-vendor dependence.
128 shinkin banks: ATM and counter outage
· Not an attack: operator says hardware failure.
Incheon Airport departure systems fail three times (30 Oct, 3 Nov, 6 Nov)
Digital bank Ueno resolved — ~2.9m accounts frozen, president impeached
· Not an attack: a solvency crisis. Lesson: concentration in one bank.
Malicious update in a security tool — ~2,950 servers
Stolen credentials at OPSSHIELD, maker of the Linux tool cPGuard, were used to push a malicious update that installed a back door and harvested password hashes and credentials.
Hosting firm Beget's cloud data wiped
A private jet from Austin to the Bahamas crashed in Palm Beach County after the pilot reported icing, turbulence and a rapid descent.

Binance loses ~$6.3bn — largest crypto theft on record

Internal wallet-signing and approval systems compromised with social engineering and malware. Binance limited withdrawals, froze some assets and said it would cover losses. On 31 Oct the FBI named North Korea-linked TraderTraitor.

Prabang hot wallet ~₩100m (24 Oct) · Bithumb mobile groupware breach, 844 customers and 715 staff (27 Oct) · Flybit, 40 customers via groupware (1 Nov) · Gopax abnormal access and extortion, trading halted (6 Nov) · Coinone via contractor (12 Nov).

A run of software supply-chain attacks in October

Chain of breaches in Korean finance — 16 firms, ~100,000 records
Supermarket fridges and freezers hacked — food thrown away

Attackers reached internet-exposed refrigeration controllers and changed temperature and defrost settings. France ~700 stores (11–12 Oct), Belgium ~40 Delhaize and ~15 Carrefour, Netherlands 17+ butchers and shops, Ireland ~13 SuperValu, Luxembourg, Sweden (set to 50°C). Germany's BSI warned on 13 Nov.

What is circulating online beside what officials have confirmed.

On 17 Nov 2026 at 2:20 pm US Eastern, FEMA and the FCC run a nationwide Emergency Alert System test (announced 16 Sep): about one minute of test messages on TV and radio. It has nothing to do with cutting power, and no official source predicts a global blackout.
'AI will shut down power and finance on a set date'
Bill Gates (Oct 2026) and the World Economic Forum warned that AI-assisted attacks may grow — a general risk, not a forecast of a shutdown on a given date.

US Army picks firms for 20+ base microreactors from 2028
The War Zone · Utility Dive · our summary

Under the Janus program the Army and DIU chose five firms to install microreactors at bases including Fort Bragg and Fort Hood from 2028 (reported up to $2.2bn). A 2022 goal calls for a microgrid at every base by 2035.
Navy tests a carrier as a floating power plant · Air Force plans microgrids at 16 bases by 2030

In May 2026 the Navy announced a demonstration of USS Gerald R. Ford powering facilities ashore. The Air Force's 2024 plan targets microgrids at 16 bases by FY2030. Marine Corps and Space Force plans, and base food arrangements, are not detailed in public reporting.

After sending the revised household brochure to every home in 2024, Sweden published a 2026 edition for businesses on their role in total defence. Households are advised to manage up to a week.

Destructive attack wiped cloud data, taking down hundreds of websites and some public services; 1,000+ servers checked by hand; some backups destroyed.

Attackers tried to change temperature and defrost settings on cooling units at three EFS plasma sites; temperature alarms let staff act at once.

Unauthenticated code execution (CVE-2026-109618/109619). Some government, school and hospital sites shut as a precaution; the November server campaign exploits this class of flaw.

Began with a commercial bank in late September. ~25,000 people via an authentication bypass in a loan-broker lookup service, plus intrusion into a staff sales system. Regulators checked 555 firms; 130 reported gaps such as missing patches and no 24-hour monitoring. Traces of an AI intrusion tool.
· Confirmed ICS intrusion; no evidence AI was used.

Combined an AI intrusion tool with an AI coding agent; attacked 60 firms over 44 days from late August and stole 8.2m+ records from ~90 companies. Also reported: a coffee chain (~2.76m records from a forgotten cloud file) and ~110,000 school learning accounts.
· Confirmed; no direct link to the finance-sector breaches.

· Crew suspected a cyberattack; under investigation.

Most household advice is 3 days; the Nordics and Japan say a week, Germany up to 10 days. The US military aims for 90 days per base.
Ottawa reminded households to keep at least three days of emergency supplies; the report counts more than 30 countries giving similar advice.

Presented at the European Civil Protection Forum in Brussels. Households should keep an emergency bag against extreme weather, cyberattacks, sabotage of infrastructure and geopolitical conflict; 72 hours lets emergency services mobilise for those most in need. Member states should teach preparedness in early schooling and include people with disabilities in plans.

Timed to the agency's launch on 2 Nov, the request goes to citizens, local governments and ministries: water, food and portable toilets for at least three days, ideally a week, and furniture secured. It restates the 2026 white paper; officials say it is not a response to any specific disaster or cyberattack. Background: Nankai Trough and Tokyo quake risk.

Seeks sites able to run 30 days without civilian utilities, with water recycling, isolated computer networks, domestic supply chains and strategic reserves. Guideline 100,000–250,000 acres; governors to present sites in spring 2027. None chosen yet.

After the UK and Japan advisories, rumours of imminent war or a huge cyberattack spread online; both are peacetime readiness campaigns. Korea has issued no new advice; the existing national guidance (a 2–3 day go-bag per person, know your shelter) applies.

Unveiled by the Defense Secretary on 30 Sep, with a program office ordered within 30 days. Planning documents call for major CONUS installations to sustain essential operations for at least 90 days without outside support: power, water, fuel and communications. Includes microreactors, large batteries, microgrids, cyber and drone defence, supply chains for munitions, medicine and blood, and domestic rare earths and chips. No cost or timeline yet; full rollout across ~500 bases could take decades.

Announced in a ministerial statement to Parliament. Households should be self-sufficient for three days against extreme weather, drought, floods, hostile-state activity and supply disruption; reported as winter-readiness rather than a war alert.
The national guide was revised; households are told to stock water and long-life food, reportedly for up to 10 days.
